slides.title: Ethereum’s and Telegram’s founders want privacy built into the apps people already use
paragraphs: Ethereum’s and Telegram’s founders want privacy built into the apps people already use
Buterin wants privacy built into Ethereum itself and Durov would rather pull Telegram’s billion monthly users out of a market than weaken its encryption.
Vitalik Buterin
Co-founder
Ethereum
“Privacy is not about standing apart. It’s about standing together.” Why I support privacy, 14 April 2025
Why privacy matters
Control over information is power, so privacy protects decentralisation, personal freedom and institutions such as the secret ballot.
What he proposes
Build privacy into Ethereum itself, covering payments, app activity, what users look up and their network identity.
What is missing today
Ethereum transactions are still public by default, and most of the plan needs wallets and apps to build it.
Pavel Durov
Founder and CEO
Telegram, over 1B monthly users
“Telegram would rather exit a market than undermine encryption with backdoors and violate basic human rights.” Telegram channel, 21 April 2025
Why privacy matters
Encryption protects everyday communication and personal safety, and any access built for authorities is also available to attackers.
What he proposes
Keep Telegram’s encryption free of government backdoors, even if Telegram has to leave a country to do it.
What is missing today
Telegram’s default chats are not end-to-end encrypted; only its opt-in Secret Chats are.
Implication Privacy that plugs into existing wallets and apps has the clearest path to users, which favours tools like Nullmask and Venice over standalone privacy chains.

slides.title: Privacy investment is accelerating as US policy turns supportive
paragraphs: Privacy investment is accelerating as US policy turns supportive

Since Tornado Cash sanctions were lifted, Venice has raised at a $1B valuation and a Zcash ETF has gathered $463M, though whether developers can be prosecuted for how others use their code is unsettled until Roman Storm’s retrial in April 2027.

Privacy investment is accelerating as US policy turns supportive
Since Tornado Cash sanctions were lifted, Venice has raised at a $1B valuation and a Zcash ETF has gathered $463M, though whether developers can be prosecuted for how others use their code is unsettled until Roman Storm’s retrial in April 2027.

details.label: 31 months under sanctions
details.description: Tornado Cash stayed on the US sanctions list from 8 August 2022 until 21 March 2025. For that period any US person who used it risked breaking sanctions law, which pushed developers and companies away from onchain privacy tools.
details.source: US Treasury; Van Loon v. Treasury

details.label: US Treasury sanctions Tornado Cash
details.description: Tornado Cash is an Ethereum mixer: users deposit into a shared pool and withdraw to a fresh address, breaking the public link between sender and recipient. On 8 August 2022 the US Treasury’s sanctions office (OFAC) blacklisted its smart contracts, saying it had laundered more than $7B since 2019, including $455M stolen by North Korea’s Lazarus Group.

details.label: Court rules code is not property
details.description: In Van Loon v. Department of the Treasury, decided 26 November 2024, the Fifth Circuit appeals court held that Tornado Cash’s immutable smart contracts are not property that can be sanctioned, because nobody owns or controls them. It put ownerless privacy code outside sanctions law at the appellate level.
details.source: US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, 26 November 2024

details.label: US Treasury lifts the sanctions
details.description: The US Treasury removed Tornado Cash from the sanctions list on 21 March 2025, so US users could interact with it again. Developer liability is still open: in August 2025 a jury convicted developer Roman Storm of conspiring to run an unlicensed money-transmitting business and deadlocked on laundering and sanctions charges, which face retrial on 26 April 2027.

details.label: Buterin and Durov
details.description: On 11 April 2025 Buterin proposed making privacy part of Ethereum’s core design, covering payments, app activity, chain reads and network-level anonymity. On 21 April Durov said Telegram would leave a market rather than build encryption backdoors for authorities. Two founders with very large user bases put privacy at the centre of their products.
details.source: Buterin, 11 April 2025; Durov’s Telegram channel, 21 April 2025

details.label: GENIUS Act
details.description: The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act, signed on 18 July 2025, is the first US federal law for payment stablecoins, setting rules for reserves, licensing and redemption. It gives banks and payment companies a legal route onto public chains, bringing payroll and supplier flows that companies normally keep confidential.

details.label: USAD and the Privacy Cluster
details.description: On 1 October 2025 Paxos Labs and Aleo announced USAD, a US dollar stablecoin whose balances and transfers are private by default. On 9 October the Ethereum Foundation formed a Privacy Cluster of 47 researchers, engineers and cryptographers to make privacy a first-class property of Ethereum.
details.source: Paxos Labs and Aleo, 1 October 2025; The Block, 9 October 2025

details.label: a16z: privacy is crypto’s moat
details.description: a16z crypto’s Ali Yahya argued that privacy will be the strongest moat for blockchains: “bridging tokens is easy, bridging secrets is hard”. A chain that holds users’ private state is harder to leave than one that holds only public balances, which favours privacy networks that gain users early.

details.label: ZEC passes $20B as its ETF fills
details.description: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF (ZCSH) began trading on NYSE Arca on 25 August 2026 and held $463.2M by 7 September, giving investors with ordinary brokerage accounts regulated exposure to a privacy coin. On that same day ZEC reached $1,249, taking its market value to about $20.4B and making it the ninth-largest crypto asset, ahead of Hyperliquid.
details.source: Grayscale; NYSE Arca, 25 August to 7 September 2026; Bitcoin.com News and Cointelegraph, 7 September 2026, citing CoinGecko

details.label: Venice Series A
details.description: Venice, the private AI platform behind VVV, raised a $65M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Dragonfly. It reported 3.5M registered users and a $100M annualised revenue run rate in August 2026 (company-reported).
details.source: TechCrunch via AI Weekly, 1 July 2026; Erik Voorhees via Phemex, August 2026

hover_details.label: Trading and tokenised assets
hover_details.description: Railgun, the main private trading protocol on Ethereum, shielded a record $1.6B in 2025 and about $4B since 2021, and the Ethereum Foundation’s Kohaku wallet toolkit integrates it. GSR executed a confidential OTC trade on the Zama protocol in March 2026, and Zama’s own token sale shielded more than $121M on Ethereum. Renegade, an onchain dark pool that hides orders until they match, has handled about $340M of volume across Arbitrum and Base since launch. Market size: about $1.6T of onchain trading and investment and $1.1T of exchange flows in 2025. Tokenised real-world assets, excluding stablecoins, were about $46B in September 2026 and McKinsey’s base case is about $2T by 2030.
hover_details.source: DL News, 21 October 2025; GSR, 12 March 2026; The Block, February 2026; BCG and Allium, January 2026; Token Terminal via Crypto Briefing, 1 October 2026; McKinsey, From ripples to waves, June 2024; DefiLlama, Renegade, October 2026

hover_details.label: Payments and payroll
hover_details.description: About 30% of all ZEC is now held in Zcash’s shielded pool, up from about 11% a year earlier. Nullmask, which adds privacy to existing wallets, reported $50M of private volume in its first three weeks. Tether made USDT available on Zama’s confidentiality layer in September 2026, and Bron paid salaries in confidential USDT on Ethereum mainnet through Zama in January 2026. Toku, a token payroll provider that has processed more than $1B of payroll, launched private stablecoin payroll on Paxos Labs’ USAD in January 2026. Market size: $390B of genuine stablecoin payments in 2025, worth about $2B a year at a 0.5% privacy fee (Khala calculation, slide 5).
hover_details.source: Delphi Digital via BIT Research, September 2026; Pinion Newswire, 19 October 2026; Tether, 15 September 2026; Zama and Bron, 16 January 2026; McKinsey and Artemis, 2025 data; Aleo, USAD case study, 21 July 2026

hover_details.label: Private connectivity
hover_details.description: Tor averaged about 3.3M directly connecting users a day from mid-September to mid-October 2026, according to the Tor Project’s own measurements. URnetwork reports 126,717 IP providers sharing bandwidth, and NymVPN runs on about 750 mixnet nodes. Both offer decentralised alternatives in which no single company sees both who a user is and what they visit. URnetwork reports about 350K monthly users of its VPN. Market size: the global VPN market was about $54.1B in 2025 and is forecast to reach about $156B by 2034, and about 6 billion people were online in 2025.
hover_details.source: Tor Metrics, 15 September to 20 October 2026; URnetwork; Nym town hall, 13 March 2026; IMARC Group; ITU, Facts and Figures 2025

hover_details.label: Private computation and AI
hover_details.description: Venice reported 3.5M registered users and a $100M annualised revenue run rate in August 2026. In June 2026 Apple extended Private Cloud Compute, which processes Apple Intelligence requests without Apple or the host being able to read them, to Google Cloud on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs with confidential computing. Phala, which runs AI models inside secure hardware enclaves, processed more than 1.34B language-model tokens of confidential inference in a single day in 2025 and had more than 1,000 teams running production workloads. Market size: confidential computing, which keeps data encrypted while it is processed, was about $24B in 2025, and Gartner predicts that by 2029 more than 75% of operations processed on untrusted infrastructure will be secured this way. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending of about $2.7T in 2026.
hover_details.source: Erik Voorhees via Phemex, August 2026; DatacenterDynamics, 10 June 2026; Fortune Business Insights; Gartner, 20 October 2025 and 16 September 2026; Phala 2025 report

slides.title: Stablecoin payments could pay about $2B a year for privacy, over half of it from businesses
paragraphs: Stablecoin payments could pay about $2B a year for privacy, over half of it from businesses

Of about $62T moved by stablecoins in 2025, 93% was bots and intermediary hops, and within the $4.2T of real activity, trading and exchange flows are seven times larger than payments, but payments are where a 0.5% privacy fee is plausible.
Businesses are the larger prize at about $1.1B a year, but consumer transfers are where stablecoins are already used most, so consumer privacy wallets may find paying users first.
The $2.7T of trading and exchange flows is a second, lower-fee market, where privacy hides positions from copy-traders and front-running bots, and which Umbra’s private swaps already serve.
These fees go to whoever processes private stablecoin flows, so Zcash and Monero holders only benefit if that activity moves onto their chains.

details.label: Bots and internal transfers: about $50T
details.description: Automated trading bots, MEV, smart-contract plumbing and wallets moving money to themselves. About 81% of all stablecoin transfers, with no buyer paying a seller.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Intermediary hops: about $7.5T
details.description: The same dollar passing through routers, bridges and contracts on the way to its destination, counted again at each step. About 12% of transfers.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Economic activity: about $4.2T
details.description: What remains after removing bots, internal transfers and intermediary hops, about 7% of all transfers. It covers trading, exchange flows and payments.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Trading and investment: about $1.6T
details.description: Stablecoins used to buy and sell crypto onchain, including about $100B of decentralised exchange flow. Traders want privacy to hide positions from copy-traders and front-running bots, but pay fees of hundredths of a percent rather than 0.5%.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Exchange flows: about $1.1T
details.description: About $700B settled inside centralised exchanges and $400B of deposits and withdrawals between exchanges and personal wallets.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Unclassified: about $0.95T
details.description: Economic transfers BCG could not assign to a category. Some is likely payments, which is why BCG calls its payment figures lower bounds.
details.source: Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

details.label: Payments: about $390B
details.description: Transfers between separate parties paying for goods, services, wages or remittances. McKinsey and Artemis put 2025 at $390B, within BCG’s $350B to $550B range.
details.source: Source: McKinsey, Stablecoins find their niche, 26 May 2026, using Artemis Analytics and the McKinsey Global Payments Map, 2025 data; Source: BCG, Stablecoin Payments: The Truth Behind the Numbers, January 2026, using Allium data for 2025

slides.title: NOCK is a bet on private money from a zero-knowledge chain, with privacy due in 2027
paragraphs: NOCK is a bet on private money from a zero-knowledge chain, with privacy due in 2027

Nockchain already secures every block with zero-knowledge proofs and plans to use the same proving system to make NOCK transfers and apps private; until the privacy pool ships in 2027, every balance and transfer is public.
What it sells Private, programmable money on a chain built around zero-knowledge proofs. Mining already produces the proofs; the 2027 roadmap applies them to private transfers and apps.
How value reaches the token NOCK is capped money with no premine or sale. Miners take 80% of issuance and all fees, so holders own a monetary asset whose privacy premium depends on the roadmap.
Supply risk About 55% of the cap is mined, much of it in the first ten months. Zorp mined at launch, owing 35% of that capture to seed investors, and the code has no third-party audit.
What has to be true The ZK opcode, privacy pool and private apps must ship on schedule in 2027, and people must then hold and move NOCK privately rather than only mine and trade it.

slides.title: Umbra’s fees reach a treasury that UMBRA holders govern, with no automatic payout
paragraphs: Umbra’s fees reach a treasury that UMBRA holders govern, with no automatic payout

Umbra hides who paid whom, and how much, on Solana, and each private transaction pays a protocol fee into a treasury that only a governance vote can direct, so UMBRA holders decide how fee income is spent but receive none of it automatically.

What it sells A private wallet for Solana that hides sender, recipient and amount on transfers and the size of swaps. It opened to the public in March 2026 with viewing keys, risk screening and geo-blocking for compliance.

How value reaches the token Fees go to a treasury account that only a timelocked vote can set, and UMBRA holders steer it through MetaDAO markets. There is no automatic buyback or dividend, so value depends on how the DAO spends.

Why the vesting matters Team and adviser tokens unlock only when fully diluted value reaches 2×, 4×, 8×, 16× and 32× the $0.30 sale price, so insider supply arrives only after the price has multiplied.

What has to be true Nimbus, the shielded pool Umbra is building for other apps, has to launch and lift deposits well beyond $187K, because treasury income grows only with the value moving through the pool.

slides.title: Venice turns AI revenue into VVV burns while cutting issuance to 2M a year
paragraphs: Venice turns AI revenue into VVV burns while cutting issuance to 2M a year

Customers pay for private AI through subscriptions, purchased credits or staked DIEM, part of that spending buys and burns VVV, and holders stake VVV to earn emissions and mint DIEM for daily API credit.

What it sells Private AI chat, images and API access to open-source and third-party models. Venice says it does not store prompts or replies, and users pick per model between private, anonymised, TEE and encrypted modes.

How value reaches the token Staked VVV earns emissions and can be locked to mint DIEM, each worth $1 of API use a day when staked. Since 17 July 2026, $5 of every $100 of credits bought has bought and burned VVV, alongside subscription burns.
Evidence of demand 3.5M registered users and a $100M annualised revenue run rate (company-reported, August 2026), after a $65M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Dragonfly.

What has to be true Burns need to outpace the 2M VVV still issued each year. API calls paid with DIEM are not credit purchases, so the burn depends on paid credits and subscriptions continuing to grow.

slides.title: Pearl verifies AI work without exposing models or data, but PRL gets no revenue
paragraphs: Pearl verifies AI work without exposing models or data, but PRL gets no revenue

Each winning piece of GPU work is wrapped in a zero-knowledge proof, so the network verifies AI computation without seeing the model weights or data inside it; customers still pay in credits rather than PRL, and PRL transfers are public.

What it sells Private AI compute: models can run on a decentralised GPU network while zero-knowledge proofs confirm the work without exposing weights or data. It is privacy for AI infrastructure, beside Venice’s privacy for users.
How value reaches the token PRL pays block rewards and fees. Customers pay for inference with prepaid credits and nothing routes that revenue to PRL, so its value rests on demand to hold it.
Supply and mining risk Only 13% of supply is mined and inflation stays near 30% in year three. Two pools reportedly find 75-80% of blocks, and three forks this summer patched mining exploits.
What has to be true Private, verifiable inference must reach paying customers, and paid demand must replace the unrequested work a June study found on most mining rigs.

details.label: Model owner
details.description: The matrices used in Pearl’s work can include “proprietary data, model weights, or sensitive user-derived information”, according to its whitepaper. The design aims to keep them confidential while the work is verified publicly.

details.label: GPU miner
details.description: Mining is matrix multiplication, the core of AI inference, so a miner can serve a customer’s request and use the same work as a mining attempt. Only NVIDIA GPUs are supported today.

details.label: Zero-knowledge proof
details.description: Winning work is wrapped in a zkSNARK so “the full protocol can be executed and verified without ever revealing the actual contents” of the input matrices. The proof does reveal matrix shapes, commitments and mining parameters.

details.label: Pearl chain
details.description: A Bitcoin-derived chain launched in April 2026. Each block carries a zero-knowledge certificate of the work and pays a block reward that decays smoothly instead of halving.

details.label: What is and is not private
details.description: Private: the matrices used in the mining work, which can hold model weights or user data. Public: PRL balances and transfers, plus the proof’s shapes, commitments and parameters. details.label: Block rewards
details.description: Block rewards started near 3,230 PRL and decay smoothly; about half of the 2.1B cap is expected by the end of 2029. Inflation is very high in year one and falls to roughly 30% by year three.

details.label: Customers
details.description: Inference customers pay per token from prepaid credits, so customer revenue does not reach PRL today. Launch prices were up to about 75% below a major provider’s standard rates.

details.label: Planned
details.description: A proof-of-inference layer is being built with Attestable to make customer inference private and verifiable, and the whitepaper describes a PRL-based compute marketplace with no launch date. Neither is live.

paragraphs: Priced deposits could create demand for UR (SN25)
Although the launch rate is zero, priced deposits would lock UR (SN25) against traffic, with revenue-funded purchases expected in the design but not enforced.
The illustrative bars show deposits exceeding miner emissions above the dotted line, without assigning a calibrated deposit rate.
Deposits lock UR (SN25) in a reserve with no outbound transfer path, but operators can fund them from existing holdings rather than new market purchases.

slides.title: UR (SN25) would be worth 11× at Helium’s market cap and 61× at Grass’s
paragraphs: UR (SN25) would be worth 11× at Helium’s market cap and 61× at Grass’s
The 23 October 2026 comparison places UR (SN25) at $7.4M, Helium at $82M and Grass at $452M on a logarithmic USD scale, illustrating relative size rather than a modelled valuation.
A wide valuation gap Transaction-privacy assets are valued at about $32B, against $32M for Nym and UR (SN25), a gap of around 1,000 times.
A product already in market URnetwork, the VPN that UR (SN25) supplies, reports about 350K monthly users and 126,717 providers across 103 countries, so the thesis does not depend on a product launch.

Demand linked to usage If a non-zero rate is adopted, usage-based deposits would lock tokens, although growing traffic would not guarantee new market buying because revenue-funded purchases are not enforced.

slides.title: UR (SN25)’s operator roadmap extends from consumer VPNs into enterprise and AI
paragraphs: UR (SN25)’s operator roadmap extends from consumer VPNs into enterprise and AI
With ur.io already live and enterprise and AI programmes still in research, the peer figures illustrate market scale rather than forecast UR (SN25) revenue.
Operators can share the miner fleet, although additional traffic still creates operating costs.
AI agents are routinely blocked by bot controls and data-centre IP detection, and residential routes are what let them reach the open web.
If these programmes become paying operators, their traffic could create UR (SN25) demand once deposits are priced.
